title: Cocycle for counit mates of coherent coefficient comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_A,\mathcal C_B,\mathcal C_C$ and $\mathcal D_A,\mathcal D_B,\mathcal D_C$ be categories, and $F_R:\mathcal C_R\rightleftarrows\mathcal D_R:G_R$ adjunctions with counits $\varepsilon_R$ for $R=A,B,C$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Let $T_{AB},T_{BC},T_{AC}$ be coefficient functors on both families, with coherent associators $T_{BC}T_{AB}\cong T_{AC}$ and identity coefficient functors. Fix objects $N_R\in\mathcal D_R$ with coherent identifications $T_{RS}N_R\cong N_S$. Let $c^{RS}:T_{RS}F_R\to F_ST_{RS}$ be natural transformations whose identity coefficient components $c^{RR}_{G_RN_R}$ equal the unit identifications, and assume that at the single object $G_AN_A$ one has $c^{AC}_{G_AN_A}=c^{BC}_{T_{AB}G_AN_A}\circ T_{BC}(c^{AB}_{G_AN_A})$ under these associators. Assume $c^{AB}_{G_AN_A}$, $c^{AC}_{G_AN_A}$, $c^{BC}_{G_BN_B}$ and $c^{BC}_{T_{AB}G_AN_A}$ are isomorphisms. Define $v_{RS}:T_{RS}G_RN_R\to G_SN_S$ as the adjunct of $(T_{RS}\varepsilon_{R,N_R})(c^{RS}_{G_RN_R})^{-1}$. Then
$$v_{AC}=v_{BC}\circ T_{BC}(v_{AB}),\qquad v_{RR}=1,$$
with the coherent identifications understood. Each equality is global in its Hom set and does not assume the $v$ are invertible.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, penultimate sentence: the same adjoint calculation proves the quotient cocycle and counit compatibility; extraction of the expanded retained stage-1 proof, steps 26

proof.text: Work under the given coherent coefficient and object identifications; write $X=G_AN_A$, $Y=G_BN_B$, $a=v_{AB}$, $b=v_{BC}$ and $T=T_{BC}$. For each pair $R,S$, the inverse Hom bijection is $w\mapsto\varepsilon_{S,N_S}\circ F_S(w)$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Thus the defining adjunct equation is $\varepsilon_S F_S(v_{RS})=T_{RS}(\varepsilon_R)(c^{RS}_{G_RN_R})^{-1}$. Equality of these transposes detects equality of maps in the entire Hom set. Here $\varepsilon_R$ means the component at $N_R$.

proof.text: Naturality of $c^{BC}:TF_B\to F_CT$ at the actual morphism $a:T_{AB}X\to Y$ gives $F_C(Ta)c^{BC}_{T_{AB}X}=c^{BC}_{Y}T(F_Ba)$. Multiplying by the two assumed component inverses yields $(c^{BC}_{Y})^{-1}F_C(Ta)=T(F_Ba)(c^{BC}_{T_{AB}X})^{-1}$. This uses only the definition of a natural transformation and inverse identities; no natural inverse transformation is asserted.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, penultimate sentence: the same adjoint calculation proves the quotient cocycle and counit compatibility; extraction of the expanded retained stage-1 proof, steps 26

proof.text:
Transpose $b\circ T(a)$ under $F_C\dashv G_C$. The counit formula from step 1, then the defining equation for $b$ and step 2, give
$$\begin{aligned}\varepsilon_CF_C(b\circ T(a))&=T(\varepsilon_B)(c^{BC}_{Y})^{-1}F_C(Ta)\\&=T(\varepsilon_BF_Ba)(c^{BC}_{T_{AB}X})^{-1}\\&=T(T_{AB}(\varepsilon_A))\,T((c^{AB}_{X})^{-1})(c^{BC}_{T_{AB}X})^{-1}\\&=T_{AC}(\varepsilon_A)(c^{AC}_{X})^{-1}.\end{aligned}$$
The third equality substitutes the defining equation for $a$. For the last, a functor preserves an inverse because applying it to the two inverse identities gives the inverse identities again; the assumed cocycle at $X$ gives $(c^{AC}_X)^{-1}=T((c^{AB}_X)^{-1})(c^{BC}_{T_{AB}X})^{-1}$. The last expression is the transpose of $v_{AC}$. Injectivity of the inverse Hom bijection proves the cocycle globally.

proof.text: For an identity coefficient change the specified unit identifications make $T_{RR}(\varepsilon_R)(c^{RR}_{G_RN_R})^{-1}=\varepsilon_R$. The inverse Hom bijection takes $1_{G_RN_R}$ to $\varepsilon_RF_R(1)=\varepsilon_R$, so its injectivity gives $v_{RR}=1$. No step cancels any $v$ or assumes that one is invertible.
